name: LISA — dark matter programme
full_name: Laser Interferometer Space Antenna dark-matter programme
summary: Space gravitational-wave mission under construction whose fundamental-physics program includes ultralight bosonic fields, black-hole superradiance, dark-matter environmental effects and primordial black holes.
detection_principle: Future low-frequency gravitational-wave waveforms and black-hole mass / spin distributions can reveal boson clouds, orbital perturbations from dark-matter environments and statistical signatures of compact dark matter.

sites.name: Planned three-spacecraft formation in heliocentric orbit
sites.location: Planned three-spacecraft formation in heliocentric orbit

status.label: Industrial development and construction underway
status.evidence: ESA signed the construction contract in June 2025; launch is planned around 2035. No LISA science data yet.

timeline.event: New Horizons for Fundamental Physics with LISA

key_parameters.name: Formation design
key_parameters.value: 3 spacecraft separated by about 2.5 million km.

key_parameters.name: Planned launch
key_parameters.value: Around 2035; planned date, not a completed launch.

results.summary: The dark-matter research concerns future sensitivities and analysis plans, not already achieved LISA dark-matter constraints.

science_scope: Dark-matter research program of a multipurpose space gravitational-wave observatory. Tests of candidate particles or black-hole environments do not automatically establish dark-matter composition; all current LISA sensitivities are forecasts.
